channel.title: Blindspot
channel.description: Independent, rigorous analysis of geopolitics, global economy, security, technology, and power. What mainstream coverage leaves out.

item.title: Behind the Abu Dhabi peace talks and the calculated sidelining of Europe
item.description: Russian and Ukrainian delegations have agreed to a major prisoner exchange in Abu Dhabi, but the exclusion of European stakeholders exposes deep fractures in the diplomatic architecture.

item.title: Apple Shutters Official Support Community Ending Decades of User-Driven Technical Knowledge
item.description: Apple has placed its official support forum in read-only mode ahead of a permanent shutdown on November 20, 2026. The move eliminates an extensive, public archive of crowd-sourced technical solutions dating back to 1998.

item.title: Nvidia Stock Hits 15-Year Relative Low as Governance Probes Target CEO Jensen Huang
item.description: Nvidia's market valuation has fallen to historic relative lows following a 5.5% stock decline. Emerging investigations into CEO Jensen Huang and debt challenges among AI infrastructure partners threaten to reprice the sector.

item.title: House Republicans Select Jim Jordan to Command Minority Caucus After Election Losses
item.description: Representative Jim Jordan of Ohio secures the top Republican leadership post in the House of Representatives. The decision signals a strategic retreat into high-intensity oversight and institutional confrontation.

item.title: CoreWeave Structuring $9 Billion in Customer Prepayments Reshapes AI Infrastructure Debt Risk
item.description: CoreWeave beat third-quarter revenue expectations while securing $9 billion in client prepayments. The novel financing strategy mitigates debt exposure but transfers structural compute risk directly to clients.

item.title: Democratic Republic of the Congo surpasses eleven thousand Ebola cases in historic outbreak
item.description: The Democratic Republic of the Congo has recorded 11,042 Ebola infections and 5,387 deaths, exposing severe structural fractures in regional health governance. The epidemic now stands as the second-largest in history.

item.title: US indicts three alleged Iranian operatives over plot targeting British airbase
item.description: Federal prosecutors charged three individuals over a plot against RAF Fairford and Jewish targets. The case underscores major vulnerabilities in prison communications security and state-sponsored proxy networks.

item.title: Senegal Pirogue Disaster Highlights Failure of Atlantic Migration Containment
item.description: At least 39 people drowned off Senegal's coast after a migrant vessel capsized near Kebemer. The catastrophe underscores how militarized maritime interdiction shifts human movement onto increasingly lethal sea routes.

item.title: Colombia earthquake survivors face institutional abandonment ninety days after disaster
item.description: Ninety days after a magnitude 7.4 earthquake shook Colombia, local officials report a total absence of central government backing. The disaster has exposed severe fractures in the national disaster response framework.

item.title: US Army soldier arrested in the United Kingdom on suspicion of Russian espionage
item.description: A senior American service member is in custody overseas facing allegations of aiding foreign intelligence. The case lays bare enduring security risks within allied defense networks.

item.title: Rising US Yields and Inflation Pressure Force Market Reassessment Ahead of December Fed Decision
item.description: Worse-than-expected inflation figures drove Treasury yields up and equities down as markets priced in tighter monetary policy. The underlying challenge remains the escalating cost of sovereign debt servicing and tightening global liquidity.

item.title: The reality behind the promise of China’s low-altitude transport sector
item.description: XPeng’s upcoming launch of a $300,000 flying vehicle marks a significant step for China’s low-altitude economy. Yet, technical limitations and restrictive regulations suggest a narrow path to mass adoption.

item.title: Behind the fog on Bulgaria's fatal Trakia motorway pile-ups
item.description: Twelve people died and fifty were injured in massive crashes on the Trakia motorway, exposing deep cracks in regional emergency response and infrastructure safety.

item.title: Inflation runs hotter than expected as higher prices extend beyond the gas station
item.description: Recent economic data shows October inflation running hotter than anticipated, with widespread price increases moving far past energy sectors. The persistent climb in core metrics challenges prevailing monetary assumptions.

item.title: The cooling of the AI boom: Analyzing the Anthropic IPO valuation
item.description: Anthropic’s push for a 1.4 trillion dollar valuation reveals a sector struggling to reconcile its massive infrastructure needs with shifting public and political sentiment.

item.title: The UK's low-gear labor market is creating a generation of economic outsiders
item.description: Bank of England deputy Clare Lombardelli warns that the current trend of low turnover is stifling mobility. While unemployment stays low, the lack of new hiring is creating a rigid economic structure.

item.title: Behind the Abu Dhabi talks and Washington's push to end the war in Ukraine
item.description: U.S. officials, Russia, and Ukraine have convened for talks in Abu Dhabi as Washington signals a strong push for peace negotiations. Beneath the diplomatic momentum lie unresolved structural conflicts over territory.

item.title: China's Trade Surplus Crosses $1 Trillion Mark Fueled by AI Demand Boom
item.description: China's trade surplus topped $1 trillion for a second year as October exports jumped 35.2%. The surge underscores Western failure to isolate Chinese electronics from global technology supply chains.

item.title: Torrential Rains Expose Structural Vulnerability of Displaced Camps in Gaza
item.description: The collapse of a rain-soaked dune onto makeshift shelters killed five people, revealing how environmental hazards compound humanitarian collapse under prolonged siege.

item.title: Trump Signals End to Iran Military Tension Following Qatari Mediated Talks
item.description: Public declarations suggest military operations involving Iran are effectively over following high-level discussions in Qatar. The shift highlights how regional diplomatic channels are working to head off broader economic fallout.

item.title: How Russia is turning attack helicopters into long-range cruise missile platforms
item.description: New footage reveals Mi-28NM helicopters firing cruise missiles designed to hit targets up to 500 km away. This tactical adaptation aims to preserve battered aircraft fleets and bypass air defenses.

item.title: Three months after Colombia's earthquake, civic solidarity exposes state absence
item.description: Ninety days after a catastrophic earthquake shook Colombia, official aid is rapidly drying up across affected regions. In the absence of state intervention, grassroots solidarity has taken over local recovery efforts.

item.title: Saudi Arabia downs missiles targeting Riyadh as pipeline attacks expose energy vulnerabilities
item.description: The interception of multiple missiles over Riyadh and a strike on the East-West oil pipeline highlight the growing exposure of critical energy transit routes amid ongoing regional conflict.

item.title: Industrial disaster in Izmir exposes critical safety vulnerabilities in Turkish steel sector
item.description: An overhead crane collapse at a metallurgical facility in western Turkey triggered a massive explosion, leaving 16 dead and five detained. Behind the official narrative of mechanical failure lies a deeper crisis of industrial oversight.

item.title: Izmir Steel Plant Explosion Kills 17 Workers Amid Industrial Safety Concerns
item.description: A crane failure dropped molten steel into a furnace in western Turkey, killing 17 workers. The disaster highlights heavy pressure on Turkey's export-driven manufacturing sector.

item.title: Market Rotation Away from Big Tech Faces Immediate CPI Inflation Test
item.description: Investors are pushing capital into sectors outside major tech firms following the US elections. Upcoming inflation figures will reveal whether this market rotation is sustainable or highly fragile.

item.title: The political calculus behind the impeachment bid against Pete Hegseth
item.description: Kentucky Representative Thomas Massie has forced a reckoning within the House of Representatives by moving to impeach the Defense Secretary. The maneuver highlights a deepening fracture in the Republican caucus following recent midterm electoral losses.

item.title: The institutional failure behind the Russell Brand conviction
item.description: Russell Brand was sentenced to 10 years and six months in prison for sexual offenses, exposing a long-standing pattern of misconduct. The trial highlights the industry's role in protecting high-value assets at the expense of accountability.

item.title: France accuses Iran of orchestrating unprecedented supermarket refrigeration cyberattacks
item.description: French authorities have blamed an Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps cyber unit for remote hacks that weaponized commercial refrigeration units. The operation highlights critical vulnerabilities in civilian retail logistics.

item.title: Trump meets Qatar prime minister in Washington amid stalled Iran war talks
item.description: United States leadership is engaging Qatari intermediaries as diplomatic channels with Iran remain deadlocked. The meetings highlight the reliance on Gulf brokers rather than direct resolution.
